recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Create `Moonseed Grove`, a mobile-first portrait browser game that preserves a rope-cut physics puzzle: a suspended object is attached by one or two cuttable ropes/vines; the player swipes across the bindings; the object falls and swings under gravity; optional collectibles add 100 points each; landing in the bottom goal wins; leaving the screen fails; restart begins a new randomized round.

The presentation should feel like a Studio Ghibli fantasy exploration miniature: painterly grove layers, drifting magic motes, handmade paper UI, a winged golden moonseed focal actor, glowing vine-charms, dew charm collectibles, and a forest spirit tea bowl goal. Keep controls touch-friendly, HUD text short, and all gameplay readable in portrait ratios from 4:7 to 9:16.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint — Moonseed Grove

## Source Truth
The preserved source is a one-screen rope-cut physics puzzle using a canvas, Verlet points/sticks, pointer swipe input, collectibles, a bottom goal, score increments, and win/fail overlays. The core mechanic is: swipe through active rope segments, let the suspended object fall/swing under gravity, collect optional stars for +100 each, land in the goal to win, or drift out of bounds to fail.

## Protected Mechanics
- Pointer/touch down starts the game from the entry overlay.
- During play, pointer drag forms a cutting trail.
- Segment intersection disables rope/vine sticks.
- Verlet gravity/friction/stiffness remain configurable with the same default values.
- 1–2 ropes in active rounds, one demo rope on the title screen.
- Three optional collectibles score 100 each.
- Goal collision uses goal radius plus object radius tolerance.
- Out-of-bounds falling is failure; goal contact is success; restart creates a new round.

## Reinterpreted World
The original Hogwarts spell-drop presentation is regenerated as a gentle enchanted-forest exploration vignette. The falling object becomes a shy moonseed spirit, ropes become hanging vine-charms, stars become dew charms, and the goal becomes a forest spirit tea bowl. The player remains a touch/swipe guide rather than a combat actor.

## Canonical Runtime
`index.html` is the new self-contained public surface with inline CSS/JS and catalog-backed remote fonts/audio. `index_old.html` is preserved as reference only.
